registered_before_reading_any_data_of: pulse-stable-refreshed (its campaign started 13:56; none of its feature, decision or trial files had been read)
hypothesis: A syscall ID that is absent from the workload's normal reference and not produced by the exec mechanism (frozen exec set E) marks the rare-syscall attack class and not a benign new process (Pulse 5.7c, 5.8h replicated on new data).

exec_set.learned_on: pulse-live-recalibrated benign-launch intervals; frozen 21/10 before 5.7c was run

primary.reference: this run's normal from campaign end + 60 s to the first worker's end (as 5.7c)

secondary.reference: only this run's selection span (90 min of normal before the first attack): the reference a live tripwire could have had
secondary.use: descriptive, same numbers reported; decides whether a live tripwire needs a longer reference carried from earlier runs

delay_definition: end of the first 500 ms window carrying a novel ID - kernel_event_at
not_claimed: the tripwire does not cover attacks without a rare syscall (anonymous_mprotect_churn, seccomp_api_probe); it is a severity signal next to Pulse, not a replacement
evidence_class: blind for the tripwire rule and E; development for the attack scenarios (self-written fixtures)
